label: late original-phase / <DEL> steps, favoured inputs (h,3,s,r,k,f,...) in sequences starting with 0/o/w/i/a
explanation: Fires only in the original phase (80% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (20%); never during copying and never at t<2. Rate rises with position (orig_idx 8 is 8x baseline) and with L, so it is a late-encoding unit. Within that window it is strongly token-modulated: input h (5.7x lift, 22% of mass), 3, s, r, k, f are favoured, and it is mostly on first occurrences of the token. It is also gated by sequence context: sequences whose first token is 0, o, w, i or a carry most activation, and the strongest examples begin with these. Behaviour looks like an additive mix of current-token and early-token contributions rather than a crisp rule: the temporal window alone (phase<=1, t>=4) has 95% recall but 4% precision; adding the token and first-token sets gives F1 ~0.33 on dev. Many active steps fall outside these sets, and many predicted steps are silent.
